answer: Each identity registers one inlet reach and locks an 80-credit bond. It releases one willow float from an umber-marked start post and files release and arrival times and reach length. An auditor recomputes speed from length and elapsed time against the inlet current table for that window; deviation over 4 percent, a reused float, or duplicated times burns the bond. First filing costs 41, the kth 41+6(k-1), the 1000th 6035; 1000 fakes pay 3,038,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-float ring fails: each float, reach, and window registers once. An honest identity pays 41 once and recovers its bond.
